visual.general_description: Six clinical photographs in two rows labelled DAY 25TH and DAY 28TH under the title Rashes evolution and resolution, with blue arrows from each top photo to the bottom photo.
visual.detailed_description: Composite of six color photographs in two rows of three under the printed title "Rashes evolution and resolution". Row labels at the left read "DAY 25TH" (top row) and "DAY 28TH" (bottom row); three blue downward arrows join each top photograph to the photograph below it. No panel letters are printed. Top row: (1) a limb segment seen from the side against a bed rail and clear IV tubing, with a white sheet below, skin dark reddish with fine pale speckles; (2) a lower limb viewed from the front lying on white linen under a grey garment edge, skin dark red-brown with patchy pale areas and fine pale speckles, with faint vertical text marks along the left edge that are illegible; (3) a close view of trunk skin with fine dark hairs, reddish brown with paler patchy areas toward the lower edge beside a grey waistband with a red stripe. Bottom row: (1) a forearm and hand lying on a teal sheet with a white and blue connector at the wrist edge, skin brown with visible fine hair; (2) a bent lower limb on white bedding with teal cloth, skin brown with hair; (3) a bare abdomen with a navel, a teal gown lifted above it and a white brief with a printed blue pattern across the lower edge, skin brown with dark hair and a faint dark midline. Compared with the top row the bottom row skin looks more uniform in tone with fewer pale patches; individual lesions are not resolvable at this resolution. No face is visible.

visual.general_description: Flowchart of an author-proposed mechanism linking carbamazepine-induced AGEP, inflammatory and hormonal responses and uncontrolled diabetes to diabetic ketoacidosis, with dapagliflozin shown by a dash-dot arrow.
visual.detailed_description: Flowchart in blue shapes with white text on a white background. At top left a rounded box reads "UNCONTROLLED DIABETES MELLITUS". At bottom left a rounded box reads "DIABETIC KETO ACIDOSIS". A solid vertical line runs from the first box down the left side to the second, ending in an arrowhead at the second. In the middle left a rectangle lists "↑ INSULIN RESISTANCE", "↑ GLYCOGENOLYSIS", "↑ GLUCONEOGENEIS" and "TRANSIENT ↓ INSULIN PRODUCTION"; below it a blue parallelogram reads "↑ BLOOD GLUCOSE LEVEL". In the centre three diamonds read "↑ INFLAMMATORY CYTOKINES", "↑ NEUROENDORCINE RESPONSE (EPINEPHRINE, GROWTH HORMONE, CORTISOL)" and "TRANSIENT BETA-CELL DYSFUNCTION"; each has a curved or straight solid arrow running left into the middle-left rectangle. At right a rounded box reads "CARBAMAZEPINE- INDUCED AGEP (SEVERE CUTANEOUS ADVERSE DRUG REACTION )" with three solid arrows ending at the three diamonds. At bottom centre a lighter blue triangle reads "dapagliflozin", with a dash-dot line that rises and turns left to an arrowhead at the lower part of the middle-left rectangle. Whether the vertical line from the diabetes box connects to the middle-left rectangle or the parallelogram, or only passes beside them, is not clear. Printed spellings (NEUROENDORCINE, GLUCONEOGENEIS, KETO ACIDOSIS) are transcribed as shown.
